title: Cutty Sark: the fastest sailing ship of all time
titleZh: 卡蒂萨克号：史上最快的帆船
overallInstruction: You should spend about 20 minutes on Questions 1–13, which are based on Reading Passage 1 below.
overallInstructionZh: 建议用约20分钟完成第1–13题；这些题目基于下方阅读文章1。
bodyParagraphs: The nineteenth century was a period of great technological development in Britain, and for shipping the major changes were from wind to steam power, and from wood to iron and steel. The fastest commercial sailing vessels of all time were clippers, three-masted ships built to transport goods around the world, although some also took passengers. From the 1840s until 1869, when the Suez Canal opened and steam propulsion was replacing sail, clippers dominated world trade. Although many were built, only one has survived more or less intact: Cutty Sark, now on display in Greenwich, southeast London.

Cutty Sark’s unusual name comes from the poem Tam O’Shanter by the Scottish poet Robert Burns. Tam, a farmer, is chased by a witch called Nannie, who is wearing a ‘cutty sark’ – an old Scottish name for a short nightdress. The witch is depicted in Cutty Sark’s figurehead – the carving of a woman typically at the front of old sailing ships. In legend, and in Burns’s poem, witches cannot cross water, so this was a rather strange choice of name for a ship.

Cutty Sark was built in Dumbarton, Scotland, in 1869, for a shipping company owned by John Willis. To carry out construction, Willis chose a new shipbuilding firm, Scott & Linton, and ensured that the contract with them put him in a very strong position. In the end, the firm was forced out of business, and the ship was finished by a competitor.

Willis’s company was active in the tea trade between China and Britain, where speed could bring shipowners both profits and prestige, so Cutty Sark was designed to make the journey more quickly than any other ship. On her maiden voyage, in 1870, she set sail from London, carrying large amounts of goods to China. She returned laden with tea, making the journey back to London in four months. However, Cutty Sark never lived up to the high expectations of her owner, as a result of bad winds and various misfortunes. On one occasion, in 1872, the ship and a rival clipper, Thermopylae, left port in China on the same day. Crossing the Indian Ocean, Cutty Sark gained a lead of over 400 miles, but then her rudder was severely damaged in stormy seas, making her impossible to steer. The ship’s crew had the daunting task of repairing the rudder at sea, and only succeeded at the second attempt. Cutty Sark reached London a week after Thermopylae.

Steam ships posed a growing threat to clippers, as their speed and cargo capacity increased. In addition, the opening of the Suez Canal in 1869, the same year that Cutty Sark was launched, had a serious impact. While steam ships could make use of the quick, direct route between the Mediterranean and the Red Sea, the canal was of no use to sailing ships, which needed the much stronger winds of the oceans, and so had to sail a far greater distance. Steam ships reduced the journey time between Britain and China by approximately two months.

By 1878, tea traders weren’t interested in Cutty Sark, and instead, she took on the much less prestigious work of carrying any cargo between any two ports in the world. In 1880, violence aboard the ship led ultimately to the replacement of the captain with an incompetent drunkard who stole the crew’s wages. He was suspended from service, and a new captain appointed. This marked a turnaround and the beginning of the most successful period in Cutty Sark’s working life, transporting wool from Australia to Britain. One such journey took just under 12 weeks, beating every other ship sailing that year by around a month.

The ship’s next captain, Richard Woodget, was an excellent navigator, who got the best out of both his ship and his crew. As a sailing ship, Cutty Sark depended on the strong trade winds of the southern hemisphere, and Woodget took her further south than any previous captain, bringing her dangerously close to icebergs off the southern tip of South America. His gamble paid off, though, and the ship was the fastest vessel in the wool trade for ten years.

As competition from steam ships increased in the 1890s, and Cutty Sark approached the end of her life expectancy, she became less profitable. She was sold to a Portuguese firm, which renamed her Ferreira. For the next 25 years, she again carried miscellaneous cargoes around the world. Badly damaged in a gale in 1922, she was put into Falmouth harbour in southwest England, for repairs. Wilfred Dowman, a retired sea captain who owned a training vessel, recognised her and tried to buy her, but without success. She returned to Portugal and was sold to another Portuguese company. Dowman was determined, however, and offered a high price: this was accepted, and the ship returned to Falmouth the following year and had her original name restored.

Dowman used Cutty Sark as a training ship, and she continued in this role after his death. When she was no longer required, in 1954, she was transferred to dry dock at Greenwich to go on public display. The ship suffered from fire in 2007, and again, less seriously, in 2014, but now Cutty Sark attracts a quarter of a million visitors a year.

sentences.text: The nineteenth century was a period of great technological development in Britain, and for shipping the major changes were from wind to steam power, and from wood to iron and steel.
sentences.translation: 十九世纪是英国技术大发展的时期；就航运而言，主要变化是动力从风力转向蒸汽，船体材料从木材转向钢铁。
sentences.structure: 并列主干以 The nineteenth century was... 定位时代，再用 for shipping 限定领域；两组 from...to... 平行呈现动力与材料的技术转型，作为全文历史背景。

sentences.text: The fastest commercial sailing vessels of all time were clippers, three-masted ships built to transport goods around the world, although some also took passengers.
sentences.translation: 有史以来速度最快的商用帆船是快速帆船：这种三桅船为运送世界各地的货物而建，不过有些也载客。
sentences.structure: 主干是 vessels were clippers；同位语 three-masted ships 解释船型，过去分词 built to... 说明目的，although 从句补充例外用途。

sentences.text: From the 1840s until 1869, when the Suez Canal opened and steam propulsion was replacing sail, clippers dominated world trade.
sentences.translation: 从19世纪40年代到1869年苏伊士运河开通、蒸汽推进逐渐取代风帆之时，快速帆船主导着世界贸易。
sentences.structure: 时间介词短语与 when 从句界定时代；主干 clippers dominated world trade 概括其鼎盛，replacing 用进行时突出转型过程。

sentences.text: Although many were built, only one has survived more or less intact: Cutty Sark, now on display in Greenwich, southeast London.
sentences.translation: 尽管建造了许多这样的船，却只有一艘大体完整地保存下来：如今在伦敦东南部格林尼治展出的“卡蒂萨克号”。
sentences.structure: Although 让步从句衬托 only one 的稀有；冒号引出唯一幸存者，now on display 是省略关系结构，交代现状。

sentences.text: Cutty Sark’s unusual name comes from the poem Tam O’Shanter by the Scottish poet Robert Burns.
sentences.translation: “卡蒂萨克号”这个不寻常的名字来自苏格兰诗人罗伯特·彭斯的诗《汤姆·奥桑特》。
sentences.structure: 主干 name comes from the poem；介词短语补出作者身份，作用是解释船名来源。

sentences.text: Tam, a farmer, is chased by a witch called Nannie, who is wearing a ‘cutty sark’ – an old Scottish name for a short nightdress.
sentences.translation: 农夫汤姆被名叫南妮的女巫追赶；她穿着一件“cutty sark”——苏格兰古语中的短睡裙。
sentences.structure: 主干 Tam is chased；同位语 a farmer、called Nannie 与 who 从句层层补充人物，破折号解释苏格兰旧称。

sentences.text: The witch is depicted in Cutty Sark’s figurehead – the carving of a woman typically at the front of old sailing ships.
sentences.translation: 这名女巫被刻画在卡蒂萨克号的船首像上——那通常是旧式帆船前端的女性雕像。
sentences.structure: 被动主干 The witch is depicted；介词短语锁定船首像，破折号后的同位说明其形态和典型位置。

sentences.text: In legend, and in Burns’s poem, witches cannot cross water, so this was a rather strange choice of name for a ship.
sentences.translation: 在传说和彭斯的诗中，女巫不能渡水，所以给船取这个名字颇为奇怪。
sentences.structure: In legend 与 in Burns’s poem 并列限定信息来源；so 引出因果结论，rather 缓和却强化“命名奇怪”的评价。

sentences.text: Cutty Sark was built in Dumbarton, Scotland, in 1869, for a shipping company owned by John Willis.
sentences.translation: 卡蒂萨克号于1869年在苏格兰敦巴顿建造，订造者是约翰·威利斯拥有的一家航运公司。
sentences.structure: 被动主干 Cutty Sark was built；地点、时间、委托对象依次后置，owned by... 说明公司所有权。

sentences.text: To carry out construction, Willis chose a new shipbuilding firm, Scott & Linton, and ensured that the contract with them put him in a very strong position.
sentences.translation: 为实施建造，威利斯选择了新的造船公司 Scott & Linton，并确保与其签订的合同让自己处于非常有利的位置。
sentences.structure: 不定式 To carry out... 前置表目的；两个并列谓语 chose 和 ensured 展示威利斯如何掌控项目，that 从句是 ensured 的宾语。

sentences.text: In the end, the firm was forced out of business, and the ship was finished by a competitor.
sentences.translation: 最终，这家公司被迫停业，船只则由一家竞争对手完工。
sentences.structure: In the end 标示结果；两个被动分句并列，以公司倒闭和对手完工构成因果收束。

sentences.text: Willis’s company was active in the tea trade between China and Britain, where speed could bring shipowners both profits and prestige, so Cutty Sark was designed to make the journey more quickly than any other ship.
sentences.translation: 威利斯的公司活跃于中英茶叶贸易，在这一行业，速度能为船主带来利润和声望，因此卡蒂萨克号被设计成比任何其他船更快完成航程。
sentences.structure: 主干 company was active...，where 从句解释速度的商业价值，so 引出设计目标；比较结构 than any other ship 强调极限追求。

sentences.text: On her maiden voyage, in 1870, she set sail from London, carrying large amounts of goods to China.
sentences.translation: 1870年首航时，它从伦敦扬帆出发，载着大量货物前往中国。
sentences.structure: On her maiden voyage 定位事件；set sail 是主干，carrying 分词结构补充伴随的货物与目的地。

sentences.text: She returned laden with tea, making the journey back to London in four months.
sentences.translation: 它满载茶叶返航，四个月便回到伦敦。
sentences.structure: 主干 She returned；laden with tea 描写满载状态，making 分词结构补充航程用时。

sentences.text: However, Cutty Sark never lived up to the high expectations of her owner, as a result of bad winds and various misfortunes.
sentences.translation: 然而，由于风况不佳和种种不幸，卡蒂萨克号从未达到船主的高期望。
sentences.structure: However 转折；live up to 是主干谓语，as a result of 引出未达预期的原因。

sentences.text: On one occasion, in 1872, the ship and a rival clipper, Thermopylae, left port in China on the same day.
sentences.translation: 有一次是在1872年，它与竞争对手快速帆船“塞莫皮莱号”同日驶离中国港口。
sentences.structure: On one occasion 锁定个案；两个船名组成并列主语，left port 是核心动作，同日出发建立公平竞赛。

sentences.text: Crossing the Indian Ocean, Cutty Sark gained a lead of over 400 miles, but then her rudder was severely damaged in stormy seas, making her impossible to steer.
sentences.translation: 横渡印度洋时，卡蒂萨克号取得了400多英里的领先，但船舵随后在风浪中严重受损，使船无法操纵。
sentences.structure: Crossing... 是时间背景；but 连接领先与受损的逆转，making... 是结果结构，说明损伤使船无法操纵。

sentences.text: The ship’s crew had the daunting task of repairing the rudder at sea, and only succeeded at the second attempt.
sentences.translation: 船员面临在海上修复船舵的艰巨任务，直到第二次尝试才成功。
sentences.structure: 主干 crew had the daunting task；of repairing... 说明任务内容，and 连接结果，only 与 second 突出艰难。

sentences.text: Cutty Sark reached London a week after Thermopylae.
sentences.translation: 卡蒂萨克号比塞莫皮莱号晚一周抵达伦敦。
sentences.structure: 简单主干 Cutty Sark reached London；after Thermopylae 把比赛结局量化为晚一周。

sentences.text: Steam ships posed a growing threat to clippers, as their speed and cargo capacity increased.
sentences.translation: 随着蒸汽船的速度与载货能力提升，它们对快速帆船构成了日益增大的威胁。
sentences.structure: 主干 Steam ships posed...；as 原因从句说明威胁随速度和载货量增长而扩大。

sentences.text: In addition, the opening of the Suez Canal in 1869, the same year that Cutty Sark was launched, had a serious impact.
sentences.translation: 此外，1869年苏伊士运河开通——也就是卡蒂萨克号下水的同一年——造成了严重影响。
sentences.structure: In addition 衔接第二重压力；同位插入语把运河开通与下水年份并置，主干 had a serious impact 点明后果。

sentences.text: While steam ships could make use of the quick, direct route between the Mediterranean and the Red Sea, the canal was of no use to sailing ships, which needed the much stronger winds of the oceans, and so had to sail a far greater distance.
sentences.translation: 蒸汽船可以利用地中海与红海之间快捷而直接的航线；但运河对依赖大洋强风的帆船毫无用处，所以帆船不得不航行远得多的距离。
sentences.structure: While 对比两类船；蒸汽船可走直线，帆船的 which 从句解释其风力需求，and so 推出必须绕远。

sentences.text: Steam ships reduced the journey time between Britain and China by approximately two months.
sentences.translation: 蒸汽船把英国与中国之间的航程缩短了大约两个月。
sentences.structure: 主干 Steam ships reduced...；between... 限定航线，approximately two months 给出幅度，直接支持第6题。

sentences.text: By 1878, tea traders weren’t interested in Cutty Sark, and instead, she took on the much less prestigious work of carrying any cargo between any two ports in the world.
sentences.translation: 到1878年，茶商已对卡蒂萨克号失去兴趣，它转而承担声望低得多的工作，在世界任意两个港口之间运送各种货物。
sentences.structure: By 1878 定位转折时间；and instead 连接“失去茶商订单”与“改运杂货”，less prestigious 作比较评价。

sentences.text: In 1880, violence aboard the ship led ultimately to the replacement of the captain with an incompetent drunkard who stole the crew’s wages.
sentences.translation: 1880年，船上暴力事件最终导致船长被一名无能的酒鬼取代，后者还偷走了船员工资。
sentences.structure: 主干 violence...led...；to the replacement 指结果，with 引出替代者，who 从句追加偷工资的恶行。

sentences.text: He was suspended from service, and a new captain appointed.
sentences.translation: 他被停职，随后任命了一位新船长。
sentences.structure: 两个被动谓语并列但第二个省略 was；句子简洁表现旧船长停职、新船长上任。

sentences.text: This marked a turnaround and the beginning of the most successful period in Cutty Sark’s working life, transporting wool from Australia to Britain.
sentences.translation: 这标志着转机，也开启了卡蒂萨克号营运生涯中最成功的时期：把羊毛从澳大利亚运往英国。
sentences.structure: 主干 This marked...；两个并列宾语是转机与新阶段，transporting... 说明该成功阶段的具体业务。

sentences.text: One such journey took just under 12 weeks, beating every other ship sailing that year by around a month.
sentences.translation: 其中一次航程不足12周，比当年其他所有参航船只快了约一个月。
sentences.structure: 主干 journey took...；beating 分词结构表示结果，与其他船的一个月差距量化优势。

sentences.text: The ship’s next captain, Richard Woodget, was an excellent navigator, who got the best out of both his ship and his crew.
sentences.translation: 下一任船长理查德·伍杰特是一位优秀的领航员，能让船和船员发挥出最佳水平。
sentences.structure: 主干 captain was an excellent navigator；who 从句用 get the best out of 具体说明他的能力。

sentences.text: As a sailing ship, Cutty Sark depended on the strong trade winds of the southern hemisphere, and Woodget took her further south than any previous captain, bringing her dangerously close to icebergs off the southern tip of South America.
sentences.translation: 作为帆船，卡蒂萨克号依赖南半球强劲的信风；伍杰特让它比此前任何船长都驶得更南，危险地接近南美洲南端外海的冰山。
sentences.structure: As 引出船型条件；主干说明依赖信风与船长南下，bringing 分词结构突出随之而来的冰山风险。

sentences.text: His gamble paid off, though, and the ship was the fastest vessel in the wool trade for ten years.
sentences.translation: 不过，他的冒险取得了回报，这艘船连续十年成为羊毛贸易中最快的船。
sentences.structure: 主干 gamble paid off 与 ship was... 并列；though 让步语气承认风险，for ten years 突出优势持续期。

sentences.text: As competition from steam ships increased in the 1890s, and Cutty Sark approached the end of her life expectancy, she became less profitable.
sentences.translation: 随着19世纪90年代蒸汽船竞争加剧，而且卡蒂萨克号接近预期使用寿命终点，它的盈利能力下降。
sentences.structure: As 从句并列交代竞争与船龄两重压力；主干 she became less profitable 给出商业后果。

sentences.text: She was sold to a Portuguese firm, which renamed her Ferreira.
sentences.translation: 它被卖给一家葡萄牙公司，该公司把它改名为“费雷拉号”。
sentences.structure: 被动主干 She was sold；which 非限定从句补充买方改名行为。

sentences.text: For the next 25 years, she again carried miscellaneous cargoes around the world.
sentences.translation: 此后25年，它再次在世界各地运输各种杂货。
sentences.structure: 时间状语 For the next 25 years 框定阶段；主干 carried... 概括全球杂货运输。

sentences.text: Badly damaged in a gale in 1922, she was put into Falmouth harbour in southwest England, for repairs.
sentences.translation: 1922年，它在大风中严重受损，被送进英格兰西南部的法尔茅斯港维修。
sentences.structure: Badly damaged... 是过去分词原因背景；被动主干 she was put into...，for repairs 表目的。

sentences.text: Wilfred Dowman, a retired sea captain who owned a training vessel, recognised her and tried to buy her, but without success.
sentences.translation: 退休船长威尔弗雷德·道曼拥有一艘训练船；他认出了它并试图购买，却没有成功。
sentences.structure: 同位语 a retired sea captain 与 who 从句说明道曼身份；recognised 和 tried 并列，but 转出失败。

sentences.text: She returned to Portugal and was sold to another Portuguese company.
sentences.translation: 它返回葡萄牙，又被卖给另一家葡萄牙公司。
sentences.structure: 两个并列谓语顺序推进船的去向与所有权变化：returned 是不及物动词的一般过去时主动用法，was sold 是被动语态。

sentences.text: Dowman was determined, however, and offered a high price: this was accepted, and the ship returned to Falmouth the following year and had her original name restored.
sentences.translation: 然而，道曼意志坚定，报出了高价；报价获接受，船于次年返回法尔茅斯并恢复原名。
sentences.structure: however 标明执着与前次失败的反差；冒号后说明高价获接受及船返航复名的连锁结果。

sentences.text: Dowman used Cutty Sark as a training ship, and she continued in this role after his death.
sentences.translation: 道曼把卡蒂萨克号用作训练船，他去世后它仍继续承担这一角色。
sentences.structure: 主干 Dowman used... 与 she continued... 并列；after his death 突出训练用途跨越船主去世。

sentences.text: When she was no longer required, in 1954, she was transferred to dry dock at Greenwich to go on public display.
sentences.translation: 1954年它不再被需要，于是被转移到格林尼治的干船坞公开展出。
sentences.structure: When 从句交代不再需要；被动主干 was transferred，介词短语 to dry dock 说明转移目的地，只有 to go on public display 是不定式目的状语。

sentences.text: The ship suffered from fire in 2007, and again, less seriously, in 2014, but now Cutty Sark attracts a quarter of a million visitors a year.
sentences.translation: 这艘船在2007年遭遇火灾，2014年又遭遇一次较轻的火灾；如今卡蒂萨克号每年吸引25万游客。
sentences.structure: but 连接两次火灾与如今盛况的逆转；less seriously 插入比较严重程度，a quarter of a million 量化年客流。

questionSections.instruction: Do the following statements agree with the information given in Reading Passage 1? In boxes 1–8 on your answer sheet, write TRUE if the statement agrees with the information; FALSE if the statement contradicts the information; NOT GIVEN if there is no information on this.
questionSections.instructionZh: 判断下列陈述是否与阅读文章1的信息一致。在答题纸1–8题处填写：TRUE（与原文一致）、FALSE（与原文矛盾）或 NOT GIVEN（原文未提供此信息）。

questionSections.instruction: Complete the sentences below. Choose ONE WORD ONLY from the passage for each answer. Write your answers in boxes 9–13 on your answer sheet.
questionSections.instructionZh: 完成下列句子。每题只能从文章中选取一个单词作答，并将答案写在答题纸9–13题处。
questionSections.wordLimitZh: 每题只能填写一个单词

questions.prompt: Clippers were originally intended to be used as passenger ships.
questions.promptZh: 快速帆船最初是打算用作客船的。

options.label: TRUE
options.text: if the statement agrees with the information

options.label: FALSE
options.text: if the statement contradicts the information

options.label: NOT GIVEN
options.text: if there is no information on this

questions.evidence: three-masted ships built to transport goods around the world, although some also took passengers
questions.explanation: 原文先给主要建造目的 transport goods，再用 although 将载客标为部分船只的附带用途；“最初用于载客”与原文相反。
questions.distractorAnalysis: originally intended 与 built to 对应，但 passenger 把主要目的偷换了；some 也不能推出全部。

questions.prompt: Cutty Sark was given the name of a character in a poem.
questions.promptZh: 卡蒂萨克号以诗中的一个人物命名。

options.label: TRUE
options.text: if the statement agrees with the information

options.label: FALSE
options.text: if the statement contradicts the information

options.label: NOT GIVEN
options.text: if there is no information on this

questions.evidence: Cutty Sark’s unusual name comes from the poem Tam O’Shanter ... ‘cutty sark’ – an old Scottish name for a short nightdress.
questions.explanation: 名字来自诗中女巫所穿短睡裙的旧称，不是人物名；人物名是 Nannie。
questions.distractorAnalysis: 把“名字来自一首诗”偷换成“以诗中人物命名”。

questions.prompt: The contract between John Willis and Scott & Linton favoured Willis.
questions.promptZh: 约翰·威利斯与 Scott & Linton 的合同对威利斯有利。

options.label: TRUE
options.text: if the statement agrees with the information

options.label: FALSE
options.text: if the statement contradicts the information

options.label: NOT GIVEN
options.text: if there is no information on this

questions.evidence: ensured that the contract with them put him in a very strong position
questions.explanation: put him in a very strong position 与 favoured Willis 同义，信息直接一致。
questions.distractorAnalysis: firm 后来倒闭是后果背景，不改变合同有利于 Willis 的事实。

questions.prompt: John Willis wanted Cutty Sark to be the fastest tea clipper travelling between the UK and China.
questions.promptZh: 约翰·威利斯希望卡蒂萨克号成为往返英国与中国之间最快的茶叶快速帆船。

options.label: TRUE
options.text: if the statement agrees with the information

options.label: FALSE
options.text: if the statement contradicts the information

options.label: NOT GIVEN
options.text: if there is no information on this

questions.evidence: Willis’s company was active in the tea trade between China and Britain ... Cutty Sark was designed to make the journey more quickly than any other ship.
questions.explanation: 茶叶贸易、中英航线与 faster than any other ship 三点共同对应题干。
questions.distractorAnalysis: 题干的 wanted 由设计目的推知，不是无依据推测。

questions.prompt: Despite storm damage, Cutty Sark beat Thermopylae back to London.
questions.promptZh: 尽管遭遇风暴损伤，卡蒂萨克号仍比塞莫皮莱号更早回到伦敦。

options.label: TRUE
options.text: if the statement agrees with the information

options.label: FALSE
options.text: if the statement contradicts the information

options.label: NOT GIVEN
options.text: if there is no information on this

questions.evidence: Cutty Sark reached London a week after Thermopylae.
questions.explanation: 原文明确晚一周到达，题干 beat 表示更早到达，方向相反。
questions.distractorAnalysis: 领先400英里发生在受损前，不能当作最终赛果。

questions.prompt: The opening of the Suez Canal meant that steam ships could travel between Britain and China faster than clippers.
questions.promptZh: 苏伊士运河开通意味着蒸汽船往返中英能比快速帆船更快。

options.label: TRUE
options.text: if the statement agrees with the information

options.label: FALSE
options.text: if the statement contradicts the information

options.label: NOT GIVEN
options.text: if there is no information on this

questions.evidence: Steam ships reduced the journey time between Britain and China by approximately two months.
questions.explanation: 运河让蒸汽船走直接航线，而帆船必须绕远；最终航程缩短约两个月，支持 faster。
questions.distractorAnalysis: 题干是因果概括，证据分布在第5段第2–4句。

questions.prompt: Steam ships sometimes used the ocean route to travel between London and China.
questions.promptZh: 蒸汽船有时会走大洋航线往返伦敦与中国。

options.label: TRUE
options.text: if the statement agrees with the information

options.label: FALSE
options.text: if the statement contradicts the information

options.label: NOT GIVEN
options.text: if there is no information on this

questions.evidence: While steam ships could make use of the quick, direct route ... sailing ships ... needed the much stronger winds of the oceans
questions.explanation: 原文只说蒸汽船可以走运河直线、帆船需要大洋强风，没有说明蒸汽船是否“有时”也走大洋航线。
questions.distractorAnalysis: 不能把帆船的 ocean route 需求转移给蒸汽船，也不能因“could”推断实际频率。

questions.prompt: Captain Woodget put Cutty Sark at risk of hitting an iceberg.
questions.promptZh: 伍杰特船长让卡蒂萨克号面临撞上冰山的风险。

options.label: TRUE
options.text: if the statement agrees with the information

options.label: FALSE
options.text: if the statement contradicts the information

options.label: NOT GIVEN
options.text: if there is no information on this

questions.evidence: bringing her dangerously close to icebergs off the southern tip of South America
questions.explanation: dangerously close to icebergs 直接对应 at risk of hitting an iceberg。
questions.distractorAnalysis: 原文没有说真的相撞，题干也只说处于风险中。

questions.prompt: After 1880, Cutty Sark carried __________ as its main cargo during its most successful time.
questions.promptZh: 1880年以后，在最成功时期，卡蒂萨克号主要运载__________。
questions.evidence: the most successful period in Cutty Sark’s working life, transporting wool from Australia to Britain
questions.explanation: most successful period 精确定位；transporting 后的 wool 是唯一符合货物名词的原文词。
questions.distractorAnalysis: cargo 等是泛称，Australia/Britain 是地点；限 ONE WORD ONLY。

questions.prompt: As a captain and __________, Woodget was very skilled.
questions.promptZh: 伍杰特既是船长，又是一名技艺高超的__________。
questions.evidence: The ship’s next captain, Richard Woodget, was an excellent navigator
questions.explanation: captain 与题干已给，excellent 对应 very skilled，缺项为 navigator。
questions.distractorAnalysis: crew 不是 Woodget 的身份；vessel 是船。

questions.prompt: Ferreira went to Falmouth to repair damage that a __________ had caused.
questions.promptZh: 费雷拉号前往法尔茅斯修理由__________造成的损坏。
questions.evidence: Badly damaged in a gale in 1922, she was put into Falmouth harbour ... for repairs.
questions.explanation: damage、Falmouth、repairs 三重定位；介词 in 后的天气名词 gale 是致损原因。
questions.distractorAnalysis: harbour 是维修地点，1922 是时间，均不回答 cause。

questions.prompt: Between 1923 and 1954, Cutty Sark was used for __________.
questions.evidence: Dowman used Cutty Sark as a training ship ... When she was no longer required, in 1954, she was transferred ...
questions.explanation: 1923年复名后由 Dowman 用作 training ship，直到1954年不再需要；填用途名词 training。
questions.distractorAnalysis: ship 已隐含于题干主语且会造成语法不合；display 是1954年之后。

questions.prompt: Cutty Sark has twice been damaged by __________ in the 21st century.
questions.promptZh: 21世纪，卡蒂萨克号曾两次被__________损坏。
questions.evidence: The ship suffered from fire in 2007, and again, less seriously, in 2014
questions.explanation: 2007与2014均属21世纪，again 表明同一原因第二次发生，答案 fire。
questions.distractorAnalysis: seriously 是程度副词，visitors 是现状，不是致损因素。
